title: Your own calendar
hookLine: a year of holidays marked in your own diary
tomorrow: what if your home could be a small sanctuary?

cards: Your phone's calendar fills itself: shifts, a dentist, a group project, a birthday it pulled from a chat. Look at next month and ask who put it all there. Mostly other people.
So who decides what goes on your calendar?
The commentator Rashi noticed something about the Torah's answer: the first command given to the Israelites as a people, still in Egypt, before they're free, is about the calendar.

teach.b: In Egypt, God tells Moses: "This month shall be unto you the beginning of months; it shall be the first month of the year to you."
Rashi, opening his commentary on Genesis, says the Torah could have started right there, with this command. Before freedom, a calendar. Slaves don't own their time; free people mark it.
A Psalm turns it into a request: "So teach us to number our days, that we may get us a heart of wisdom."
So the practice is quiet and almost like paperwork: open next year and mark the festivals before anyone else fills the dates.
Then mark your own days beside them: a yahrzeit, a beginning, a friend's loss you don't want to forget. The year is yours because you said what it's for.

teach.h: ONE MOON, TWO WAYS TO KEEP TIME.
teach.b: A neighbor tradition reads the moon as a clock too. The Qur'an says of the new moons, in Pickthall's translation: "They are fixed seasons for mankind and for the pilgrimage."
Jewish months and Muslim months both begin with the new moon.

And the honest difference: the Jewish calendar adds a month in some years, so that Passover stays in spring, the month of Abib; the Islamic calendar adds none, so Ramadan moves through the seasons over the years.
The same moon, two faithful ways of keeping time.

how: Some Jews keep a printed Jewish calendar (a luach) or mark the festivals, fast days and family yahrzeits in their own planner at the start of the year.

practice: Open a calendar, paper or phone, to next year. Mark one festival you want to keep, and one date that's yours alone: a yahrzeit, a beginning, someone you don't want to forget.
Write each one in your own words, not the app's, and look at the two dates side by side.

carryVoice: Something to hold: the year is yours, once you've said what it's for. That's the year, lived.
